newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to force Spain to solve mobile phone fee row.
newsitem.headline: EU to force Spain to solve mobile phone fee row.

text.p: The European Commission is to use special powers on Wednesday to force Spain to settle a dispute about a 85-billion-peseta fee charged on the Airtel consortium for operating the country's second mobile phone licence.

Under the terms of the long-awaited ultimatum, Spain will have to reimburse the fee paid by the consortium or charge Telefonica de Espana, which was the first mobile phone operator, to pay a similar amount, Commission sources said on Tuesday.

In a last-ditch effort to solve the dispute amicably, the Commission urged the Spanish government in October to persuade the two rival companies to agree on a compromise that would compensate Airtel for the licence fee paid in 1995.
This could consist in special conditions and prices for Airtel to interconnect with Telefonica's network.

The Commission will be using article 90 of the treaty of Rome which allows it to take appropriate steps to correct distortions of fair competition. The dispute may ultimately end in the European Court of Justice.

Airtel is a consortium of banks, including Banco Central Hispano and Banco Santander, and other industrial and telecommunications partners, notably Airtouch Communications Corp and British Telecommunications Plc.
The Commission was able to restore fair competition in similar disputes in Italy, Belgium, Austria and Ireland.

In June, the Belgian government asked the local telecoms operator Belgacom to pay nine Belgian francs to match the licence fee that the country's second mobile phone operator Mobistar agreed to pay to enter the market. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
